# Citation

Ono, Y., et al. (2013). *PBSIM: PacBio reads simulator - toward accurate genome assembly*. Bioinformatics. DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/bts649. Source: [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23129296/](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23129296/).

# One-Sentence Summary

Introduces PBSIM for simulating PacBio reads to support genome-assembly evaluation.

# Scope for simitall

Use as a long-read backend for CLR or CCS-style benchmark scenarios where its installed version supports the requested data type. Persist data type, model, coverage, length behavior, and seed.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Long-read simulation should distinguish read technology or accuracy regime.
- Coverage alone is insufficient: length and error behavior determine repeat resolution.
- A known simulated reference permits assembly evaluation against truth.

# Inputs to Specify

- Reference FASTA
- Read type or error model
- Depth, prefix, and seed

# Expected Outputs

- Long-read FASTQ and simulator artifacts

# Limitations and Guardrails

- PBSIM command-line options vary between versions.
- A CCS-like simulation is an approximation and should be described with the exact tool version and model.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- Why should CLR and HiFi-like simulations be analyzed separately?
- Which long-read parameters should be stored for a hybrid-assembly benchmark?
